text:
alex: Heads-up — saw two OOMs within the last 24h on g3-12 while running long-context chat tests (seq len ~32k). KV cache used jumped ~2.5x right before OOM, process killed by OOM killer.

maria: ugh. Any recent changes to kernel selection or batching?

alex: Noticed we flipped a heuristic last week to prefer bigger batch kernels for throughput (PR #492). Think that increases temporary KV allocations when lots of prefixes are hot.

sam: Can you paste the oom / dmesg snippet?

alex: Sure — from the node:

```
Out of memory: Kill process 4231 (runtime) score 123 or sacrifice child
Killed process 4231 (runtime) total-vm:15824360kB, anon-rss:14523040kB, file-rss:0kB
```

Followed by runtime log: "kv_cache_mem=12.8GB -> 33.1GB in 7s"

jen: Perf data I pulled: alloc profile shows spike in slab allocations attributed to KV page objects. Also saw increased mutex contention on kv-slab allocator.

perf-bot: perf report attached (summary): top symbols: kv_page_alloc, kv_cache_touch, batch_assemble.

maria: So two levers: reduce KV residency or reduce transient allocs when batching. Immediate mitigation ideas?

sam: Short-term: revert the aggressive batch kernel switch or add a conservative cap when live long contexts > X tokens. Medium-term: tune eviction to prioritize compacting fragmented slabs before full-page eviction.

alex: Revert is doable but will cost throughput. Could we instead add a fallback path: when KV memory > 80% of target, switch to a "streamed-keys" mode that keeps only most recent prefixes in memory and fetches older prefixes from a compressed store (or evicts lazily)?

jen: We have a half-baked compressed page store (experimental). I can wire a fallback switch to route to that path on mem pressure, but needs safety checks. ETA: ~1d to make non-experimental.

maria: Ops suggestion: add a runtime circuit-breaker that rejects new long-context requests when free KV pages < threshold and spin up a degraded model variant that uses reduced KV footprint (e.g., lower kv-size or fewer kv-shards).

sam: Also add retry semantics: SDK should get a specific 429-ish error "kv_cache_pressure" so callers can decide to back off or switch to shorter context.

alex: Good. For immediate patch: (1) add a guard to KV allocator to refuse huge burst allocations and fallback to compacted allocation path; (2) add rejection/error code for callers; (3) schedule revert of batch-heuristic if we see recurrence.

jen: Pushing a small tweak now: limit per-request prefetch to 2x vs 4x when sequence length > 16k. Will monitor.

ops-bot: alert created: #INC-2026, paging/kv OOM, nodes affected: g3-12, g3-13. Assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

sam: Action items:
- jen: push the prefetch cap change and monitor for 24h (jen)
- alex: add circuit-breaker proposal + simple SDK 429 contract doc (alex)
- maria: run long-context stress with perf instrumentation to validate allocator change (maria)
- jen/sam: start a small canary to flip batch kernel back if incidents recur (jen, sam)

alex: I'll also draft a short runbook for graceful degradation: steps to detect kv pressure, API error codes, emergency toggle to force compressed-store fallback, and rollback path.

maria: Thanks — please add the perf traces and allocator heapshot to the ticket.

sam: +1. If this mitigates, we can follow-up with deeper work: smarter reuse heuristics to avoid fragmentation (coalesce free ranges) and a background compaction job during idle windows.

alex: Agreed. Keeping this thread for updates. Ping me if the canary shows any new OOMs. :thumbsup:
